# Ridu

This application was generated by Ridu. Its executable Go configuration is the source of truth.

**New to Ridu? Start with [`PROJECT.md`](./PROJECT.md).** It explains what every generated file is
for, which files are yours to edit, and which files Ridu owns.

- Go module: `example.com/ridu-dogfood`
- Project template: `blank`
- Database: `postgres`
- Generated client: `generated/ridu.generated.ts`
- Ridu release: `v0.0.0-dogfood.1788901341006834000`

If coding-agent guidance was selected, the project includes complete local `ridu-project` and
`payload-to-ridu` skills. They work offline and match this CLI release. Keep project-specific notes
in `PROJECT.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `CLAUDE.md`, and run `bun run ridu -- agent sync` after upgrading Ridu.

```sh
bun install
bun run dev
```

The exact matching `@riducms/cli` is a project-local development dependency. Ridu starts the
development database, keeps generated
contracts current, runs the Go API and Vite admin together, and prints the local URLs. Edit
`content/*.go` to change your CMS. Schema changes reload the open admin after the new Go server is
ready; Svelte component changes use Vite hot module replacement.

If you enable the optional GraphQL plugin, configure `generated.graphql.schema` in `ridu.toml` so ordinary
generation also commits and drift-checks its exact SDL for client tooling.

On an empty database, open the admin and create the first `users` account in the guided setup
screen. Ridu serializes that anonymous first-user operation with the credential write, so exactly
one contender can succeed. Afterward, the generated collection policies require authentication;
anonymous registration is not enabled accidentally. See `PROJECT.md` for the non-interactive REST shape and for how to opt into
intentional public registration.

Before release:

```sh
bun run ridu -- migrate create --name initial
bun run ridu -- generate --check
bun run ridu -- check
bun run ridu -- migrate verify
bun run ridu -- build
```


The production artifact is `dist/ridu`. Production needs only that binary and its
environment variables; Bun and Node.js are build-time dependencies. Inspect
`bun run ridu -- migrate plan --json` and apply `bun run ridu -- migrate up` with the exact release and committed artifacts before starting the new
binary. Follow the production boundary and cutover checklist in `PROJECT.md`.

If `ridu new` retained this project after dependency or generation setup failed, fix the reported
error and finish initialization with `go mod tidy && bun install && bun run ridu -- generate`
before starting development.
